name: Jalisco

standard.note: The 'Cabañas' plate is white with a row of little orange-and-blue icons up top (the Hospicio Cabañas dome, the state seal and an agave) and a QR code in the corner.

plates.title: Current design (2025)
plates.fact: The 'Cabañas' plate is white with a row of little orange-and-blue icons up top (the Hospicio Cabañas dome, the state seal and an agave) and a QR code in the corner.

plates.title: 'Collage' design (2019-2025)
plates.fact: Collage plates meet the federal standard, so they stay legal alongside the new Cabañas plates.

plates.title: Vehicles for people with disabilities
plates.fact: Jalisco issues special plates for vehicles adapted for, or used to carry, people with disabilities.

plates.title: Ecological vehicles (green plate)
plates.fact: Hybrid and electric cars in Jalisco can carry a green plate.

notes: Only Collage (2019) and Cabañas (Feb 2025) are legal. The older Minerva, Gota and Maguey plates had to be swapped; the last free-swap deadline was 29 May 2026 (hacienda.jalisco.gob.mx release, 27 Mar 2026), so they should be off the road now. The standard picture is a government photo of the plate held in someone's hands (cropped 16:9). The disability and green-plate entries come from a Google snippet of the trámite JAL-SET-0008 (the page didn't render for me) and the Ley de Movilidad, which mentions 'vehículos híbridos o eléctricos con placa verde'. No pictures or start years found for them. I found no official Collage picture.
